mechanism: When recent volatility is low, aggregate load follows a stable daily calendar shape, so same-hour historical segments are more predictive than volatile periods.
failure_condition: during high volatility, holidays, or sudden load shifts
retrieval_action: Prefer historical segments with the same hour_of_day and down-weight segments from dissimilar volatility regimes.
expected_effect: The retrieved futures should match the regular time-of-day load shape and avoid volatile anomalies.
reason: Low recent volatility signals a smooth, calendar-dominated regime; time-of-day is the strongest predictor for aggregate load in such periods.
claim: When recent volatility is low, aggregate load follows a stable daily calendar shape, so same-hour historical segments are more predictive than volatile periods.

mechanism: Morning ramps are dominated by a consistent start-of-day load pickup, so high recent slope in the morning is best matched to same-hour historical segments across both workdays and weekends.
activation_condition: when recent_slope_magnitude is high and hour_of_day is morning
failure_condition: when the ramp is not a structural morning pickup (e.g. weather-driven or late-start) or recent_slope_magnitude is low
retrieval_action: Prefer historical segments with the same hour_of_day and similar recent_slope_magnitude, but cross working_day instead of matching day type.
expected_effect: Retrieved futures should capture the typical morning ramp shape and duration without over-restricting to the current day type.
reason: Morning ramp shape is largely driven by hourly start-up behavior; matching slope and hour while crossing day type increases analog availability and reduces unstable day-type restrictions.
claim: Morning ramps are dominated by a consistent start-of-day load pickup, so high recent slope in the morning is best matched to same-hour historical segments across both workdays and weekends.

mechanism: Non-working days have a distinct lower and later-starting load profile from workdays, so restricting to non_working history matches that structure.
failure_condition: when a non-working day is distorted by an event or weather that dominates the usual weekend profile
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to non_working historical segments and prefer the same hour_of_day.
expected_effect: Should align retrieved futures with reduced commercial/industrial load and a different diurnal shape on non-working days.
reason: Workday and non-working day load composition differ systematically; matching non_working status avoids structural mismatch that occurs when weekday history is allowed.
claim: Non-working days have a distinct lower and later-starting load profile from workdays, so restricting to non_working history matches that structure.

mechanism: On weekends, aggregate load lacks much of the workday industrial/commercial demand, so weekend history is more predictive and workday history can be misleading.
failure_condition: on workdays or during special events that mimic workday load patterns
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to weekend/non-working historical segments and prefer the same hour_of_day.
expected_effect: Retrieved futures should match the lower, smoother weekend load profile instead of importing workday peaks.
reason: The day-type composition change is a first-order effect for aggregate electricity load; restricting to non-working days prevents structural mismatch.
claim: On weekends, aggregate load lacks much of the workday industrial/commercial demand, so weekend history is more predictive and workday history can be misleading.

mechanism: In summer and winter, seasonal heating/cooling demand creates distinct load level and shape regimes, so same-season historical segments are more predictive.
activation_condition: when seasonal_level is summer or winter
failure_condition: in spring/autumn transition periods or when weather deviates strongly from seasonal norms
retrieval_action: Prefer historical segments from the same seasonal_level and with similar recent_level.
expected_effect: Retrieved futures should match seasonal demand intensity and avoid cross-season shape mismatches.
reason: Heating and cooling loads dominate winter/summer and shift both level and intraday patterns; seasonal matching reduces this mismatch.
claim: In summer and winter, seasonal heating/cooling demand creates distinct load level and shape regimes, so same-season historical segments are more predictive.
